title: Kansas football great Tony Sands gave a fan the Heimlich before KU-Missouri rivalry game
content:
When Tony Sands saw a fan clutching his throat and gasping for air, he didn’t stop to ask if the guy was rooting for Kansas or Missouri.

The young man wouldn’t have been able to answer anyway.

“He had his hand by his throat in the choking procedure, and he couldn’t say nothing,” said Sands, a star running back for the Jayhawks who rushed for 396 yards on a Football Bowl Subdivision-record 58 carries against Missouri in 1991. “As he started to turn red, I knew then that he was choking.”

Sands was in Lawrence, Kan., to sign copies of his book and display the football from his record-setting game before last Friday’s installment of the Border War, a heated and historic rivalry with roots in the Civil War.

Sands was packing up his pregame tailgate when his wife called his name and motioned to the young man in obvious distress. Fred Tigner, Sands’ cousin, was there with him and said he witnessed Sands’ quick reflexes.

“Tony sprung right into action,” Tigner said. “He didn’t hesitate. He gave the man the Heimlich. He definitely saved his life.”

Sands runs a training company for young athletes from his home in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., and is trained in first aid and CPR. He kept up with his certifications in case he needed to help someone in distress, though he didn’t imagine using his training in this particular setting.

“A tailgate would have been the last place I would have thought about having to perform this procedure,” Sands said. “You never know. That’s why you’ve always got to be ready and have your training.”

Once the young man was breathing again, Sands left him in the care of a police officer and continued packing up his tailgate. He didn’t think to get the man’s name or contact information, and he’s not sure whether the fan realized that the person who saved him is a member of the Kansas football ring of honor and the No. 3 rusher in school history.

“I don’t know if it dawned on him,” Sands said. “I’m quite sure for him, he was thinking about, ‘How am I going to take my next breath?’”

The night ended in disappointment for the Jayhawks, who fell 38-21 to their cross-border rivals. The bitterness between the two sides was evident after the game as Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz, upset about a pregame video that villainized Missouri with reference to the sacking of Lawrence by Confederate guerillas, said his team “left Kansas bleeding again.”

Throughout the game, Sands’ thoughts kept turning back to the fan he rescued. As he boarded his flight home the next day, he decided to put out a call on social media to see if he could locate the young man and check on his condition.

The young man was mostly likely a student at Kansas, though Sands doesn’t know for sure. In a situation that demanded quick action, Sands wasn’t thinking about the rivalry.

“I didn’t think, ‘Was he Missouri? Was he KU?’” Sands said. “I just said, ‘Listen, I gotta save this young man’s life, and I’m gonna do whatever it takes within my power to get it done.’”
